items.q: You must set bit 3 of an 8-bit register PORTB to 1 without changing the other bits. Which line does it?
items.explain: OR-ing with a mask that has only bit 3 set forces that bit to 1 and leaves every other bit as it was.

items.q: Which line clears only bit 5 of register REG?
items.explain: AND with the inverted mask keeps all bits except bit 5, which is forced to 0.

items.q: An 8-bit timer is clocked from 16 MHz through a prescaler of 64. How long between two overflow interrupts?
items.explain: 16 MHz / 64 = 250 kHz, so each tick is 4 µs and 256 ticks take 1.024 ms.

items.q: Datasheet excerpt for CTRL (8-bit): bit 7 EN (1 = enable); bits 5:4 MODE (00 off, 01 continuous, 10 single); bit 0 START. Which line enables the block in single mode and starts it?
items.explain: EN = 0x80, MODE 10 puts a 1 in bit 5 = 0x20, START = 0x01; together 0xA1.

items.q: Which of these is bad practice inside an interrupt service routine?
options: Calling printf() to log the event
items.explain: An ISR should be short; printf is slow and may not be re-entrant, so it blocks other interrupts and can corrupt state.

items.q: A UART link runs at 9600 baud with 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit. What is the maximum number of bytes per second?
items.explain: Each byte needs 10 bits on the wire (start + 8 data + stop), so 9600 / 10 = 960 bytes per second.

items.q: An I2C EEPROM has 7-bit address 0x50. What is the first byte the master sends to start a write to it?
items.explain: The address byte is the 7-bit address shifted left with the R/W bit in bit 0; 0x50 << 1 = 0xA0 and write means bit 0 = 0.

items.q: A sensor datasheet says: clock idles low; data is shifted out on the falling edge and must be sampled on the rising edge. Which SPI mode do you configure?
items.explain: Idle low means CPOL = 0, and sampling on the first (rising) edge means CPHA = 0.
